Let  
\[
u=\frac{\cos\alpha}{\cos\beta},\qquad v=\frac{\sin\alpha}{\sin\beta}.
\]
Then \(u+v=-1\), so \(v=-1-u\).

Writing \(B=\cos^2\beta\) and \(D=\sin^2\beta\), the unit-circle conditions give
\[
(u^2-1)B+(v^2-1)D=0,\qquad B+D=1.
\]
Solving yields
\[
B=\frac{u(u+2)}{2u+1},\qquad D=\frac{1-u^2}{2u+1}.
\]
The desired expression becomes
\[
\frac{\cos^3\beta}{\cos\alpha}+\frac{\sin^3\beta}{\sin\alpha}
=\frac{B}{u}+\frac{D}{v}.
\]
Substituting \(v=-1-u\),
\[
\frac{B}{u}+\frac{D}{v}
=\frac{u+2}{2u+1}+\frac{u-1}{2u+1}
=1.
\]
